paragraphs: This is a placeholder consent form for the Meridian Timepieces pilot. It must be replaced with the approved ethics documentation before any real participant takes part.

You are invited to take part in a study about how the organisation of an online watch catalogue affects searching. Plan for about 20 minutes for the study, including setup and questionnaires. Take the time you need to read the consent information and finish the activities. You will browse a fictional store, complete short check-ins about how you feel, and answer questionnaires.

You will also complete short mood exercises: a short clip of two puppies playing, quick watch searches that may be too short to finish, a watch search that may be hard to complete, and a repetitive catalogue task. These are mild and temporary.

The study also uses webcam-based eye tracking during the scored search trials. That needs a separate consent step after this one, and you can refuse it and still complete the study. Gaze positions and timing are stored separately from your clicks and questionnaire answers. Raw video is never recorded or stored, and the study does not infer emotion from your face or gaze.

Your responses are pseudonymous: we store a participant code, not your name. Clicks and sampled cursor positions during searches, demographic answers, questionnaire answers, and separate gaze files are stored on this research computer. Gaze files have restricted researcher access and are deleted if you withdraw.

You can pause or stop at any time without giving a reason. If you feel uncomfortable, choose the visible Stop control and the session will end immediately with a debrief. You may withdraw your data at the end of the session.
There are no known physical risks. Some induction tasks are deliberately mildly frustrating, confusing, or boring. They last at most 60 seconds and are followed by a check-in and a neutral reset.
By continuing you confirm that you have read this placeholder information, that your questions have been answered, and that you agree to take part.
This is a separate consent for eye tracking. The core study consent above is not enough on its own.

The pilot uses the camera in this computer to estimate where you look during the scored search trials. The camera starts only after you agree here. It does not record video, images, or audio, and no face images leave the browser.

Gaze coordinates, timing, calibration results, and screen geometry estimated from the browser are stored in a separate restricted dataset. They are not mixed into the click-event log or questionnaire tables. Researchers can export them only from the password-protected console.

Webcam eye tracking is less accurate than a dedicated research tracker. A nine-point calibration and accuracy check measure how accurate it is for you. That result is stored with your gaze data, and the researchers decide later which recordings are accurate enough to analyse.
You can refuse now and continue without eye tracking, or stop at any time. Withdrawal deletes the gaze files together with the rest of the session data.
